Many "best web-based LIMS" lists mix cloud-native products with legacy systems that simply offer hosting. The difference decides who runs upgrades, how fast you go live, and how much IT effort you carry. This guide compares nine browser-based LIMS platforms using details from each vendor's own website, checked in November 2026. For a broader list that includes on-premises systems, see our guide to the[top LIMS vendors](https://www.scispot.com/blog/top-lims-vendors) .


## What Makes a LIMS Web-Based?


A web-based LIMS is used through a browser, with no desktop client to install. Vendors usually deliver it in one of three ways:


- **Multi-tenant SaaS:** the vendor runs one continuously updated application for all customers.
- **Single-tenant or private cloud:** the vendor or a partner hosts a dedicated instance, often chosen for validated GxP work.
- **Customer cloud:** you run the vendor's software in your own cloud account and manage more of the stack.


Labels vary between vendors, so ask who hosts, who patches, and who controls upgrade timing. For the basics, read[what cloud-based LIMS solutions are](https://www.scispot.com/blog/what-are-cloud-based-lims-solutions) .


### How we evaluated each platform


- Deployment model and who manages infrastructure and updates
- Core LIMS depth: samples, workflows, results, and reporting
- Instrument and system integration (APIs, file parsing, connectors)
- Compliance support: audit trails, e-signatures, permissions, and validation documentation
- Pricing transparency and data portability

### 1. Scispot


Scispot is an AI-native laboratory platform with expert delivery.[Scispot LIMS ++](https://www.scispot.com/lims) is a cloud-native web-based LIMS that runs inside[Scispot LabOS](https://www.scispot.com/labos) , which connects samples, inventory, workflows, instruments, and quality rules in one governed data layer.


- **Notable capabilities:** sample tracking with metadata and barcoding, configurable labflow automation, audit trails, user permissions, and configurable reports.[Scispot GLUE](https://www.scispot.com/glue) moves raw files, results, and metadata between instruments, apps, databases, and cloud platforms.[Scibot](https://www.scispot.com/scibot) AI agents search, analyze, and report on governed lab data.
- **Works alongside your stack:** add[native apps](https://www.scispot.com/native-apps) such as[ELN ++](https://www.scispot.com/elns) or QMS ++, or connect the ELN and LIMS you already run. Open APIs, an MCP server, and exports keep data portable.
- **Pricing:** custom annual pricing based on lab outcomes, with unlimited users and no per-seat fees ([Scispot pricing](https://www.scispot.com/pricing) ).
- **Best for:** biotech, diagnostics, and R&D labs that want LIMS, ELN, instrument data, and AI on one connected foundation.


### 2. QBench


[QBench](https://www.scispot.com/blog/qbench-review) describes itself as a cloud-based, highly configurable LIMS with no-code tools. It bundles LIMS with QMS, inventory, a customer portal, billing, reporting, and analytics, plus an open REST API. QBench states that it supports 21 CFR Part 11 and is[ISO 17025](https://www.scispot.com/blog/iso-17025-compliance-guide-requirements-software-best-practices) compatible.


- **Pricing:** published; plans start at $16,500 per year, including five users.
- **Best for:** testing labs that want configurable workflows and a client portal.


### 3. CloudLIMS


CloudLIMS markets web-based SaaS LIMS software for biobanks, clinical, research, and analytical testing labs, and now positions itself as AI-native. Subscriptions include workflow configuration, instrument data import, CoA and report templates, legacy data migration, a built-in QMS, patient and client portals, and automated backups.


- **Pricing:** published per user per month, billed annually, tiered by lab type and user count.
- **Best for:** biobanks and testing labs that want predictable subscription pricing.


### 4. Labguru


[Labguru](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labguru-review) combines LIMS, ELN, inventory, and sample management in one cloud platform, with audit trail and e-signature support. For GxP work, Labguru Validated Cloud offers multi-tenant or dedicated single-tenant instances with validation documentation and a PQ test environment.


- **Pricing:** not published; Labguru offers a free trial and demos.
- **Best for:** research teams that want ELN and LIMS in one place.


### 5. Benchling


[Benchling](https://www.scispot.com/blog/benchling-review) is a cloud-based R&D platform for biotech. Its Notebook, Registry, and Inventory apps link entities, samples, storage locations, and results, with barcode and instrument integrations. Benchling Validated Cloud provides a dedicated tenant with built-in controls for 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11.


- **Pricing:** not published.
- **Best for:** biotech R&D teams that organize work around registered biological entities.


### 6. LabVantage


[LabVantage](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labvantage-review) offers its LIMS, alongside ELN, LES, and SDMS, as SaaS in Standard and Enterprise tiers or on-premises. SaaS runs on an annual subscription with pre-packaged industry solutions.


- **Pricing:** not published.
- **Best for:** pharma and biotech, biobanking, diagnostics, food and beverage, and contract testing labs.


### 7. LabWare


[LabWare](https://www.scispot.com/blog/labware-review) offers three cloud options: LabWare SaaS on a monthly subscription (availability varies by region), hosting by a certified provider, or deployment in your own cloud. On-premises installation is also available.


- **Pricing:** not published.
- **Best for:** enterprise and multi-site labs.


### 8. STARLIMS


[STARLIMS](https://www.scispot.com/blog/starlims-review) offers on-premises installation, managed cloud hosting, and a cloud subscription. Its cloud options run on AWS and are accessed through a web browser, and its LIMS connects with STARLIMS SDMS, LES, ELN, and analytics.


- **Pricing:** not published.
- **Best for:** labs that want one vendor across LIMS, SDMS, LES, and ELN.


### 9. Veeva LIMS


Veeva LIMS is a cloud LIMS built for life sciences quality control. Veeva positions it to unify QC with QA and manufacturing quality processes.


- **Pricing:** not published.
- **Best for:** biopharma QC labs working under GMP.


## How to Choose the Right Web-Based LIMS


### Match the platform to your lab type


- **Testing and contract labs** that need client portals, CoAs, and billing often start with QBench or CloudLIMS.
- **Biotech R&D teams** that need ELN and LIMS together usually compare Scispot, Benchling, and Labguru.
- **Enterprise and GMP QC labs** tend to evaluate LabWare, LabVantage, STARLIMS, and Veeva LIMS.
- **Labs connecting many instruments and systems** , or preparing data for analytics and AI, should look closely at Scispot.


### Pilot one real workflow


Run one real sample end to end: intake, aliquots, a real instrument file, review, and a report. Ask each vendor to connect one instrument during the evaluation. Our[LIMS vendor selection framework](https://www.scispot.com/blog/the-complete-guide-to-lims-vendor-selection-a-data-driven-evaluation-framework-for-lab-leaders) gives you a scoring method.


### Ask the cloud-specific questions


- Is it multi-tenant or single-tenant, and who controls upgrade timing?
- What validation documentation does the vendor supply, and what stays your responsibility?
- Where is data hosted, and how do backup and disaster recovery work?
- How do you export all data and audit trails if you leave?
- What is the full cost across subscription, implementation, integrations, and validation? See our[LIMS implementation cost breakdown](https://www.scispot.com/blog/lims-implementation-cost-the-full-breakdown-and-what-to-expect) .


No web-based LIMS makes a lab compliant on its own. Your team still validates intended use and controls its processes, as covered in our guide to[21 CFR Part 11-ready LIMS](https://www.scispot.com/blog/is-your-lims-really-21-cfr-part-11-compliant-or-just-part-11-ready) .
